_provenance: AUTHORED source of truth for the Operator's Dashboard — the program-level metrics the book steers by. book-models/metrics_dashboard_model.py projects the qualifying subset into the back-matter page's table and holds the page equal to this model with a parity check (run `python3 book-models/metrics_dashboard_model.py verify`). Edit a metric HERE, then regenerate the page table with `... table`. The book's own declared -> generated idiom, applied to its metrics.
inclusion_criterion: A metric belongs in the dashboard iff it is a useful agent-loop metric OR an org-level target for engineering with MAGE — not merely a number the book measures. Diagnostics and payoff-measurements you don't steer by are out.

metrics.name: Support ratio
metrics.counts: Support-apparatus lines of code (tests, lints, load-bearing docs, agent infrastructure, tooling) divided by production lines of code.
metrics.informs: Whether to invest in the environment before the product. Watch that the apparatus keeps leading as feature work resumes.
metrics.healthy_direction: Leads production; settles around 3x it at maturity.
metrics.rationale: An org-level target: build the environment first, expect ~3x at maturity. The whole book's ordering argument, drawn as a line.

metrics.name: Missing-Model Metric
metrics.counts: The fraction of tests whose exercised code traces to no model claim — the unmodelled surface — plus its drain curve run over run.
metrics.informs: Which code to model next. Run the tracer after each model-loop Epic and watch the biggest orphan cluster shrink.
metrics.healthy_direction: Drains toward the 10%-or-under target (56% to 7.89% over nine re-runs).
metrics.rationale: A loop target with a stated goal: drain the orphan rate toward 10% or under. You steer the model-loop by it.

metrics.name: Velocity
metrics.informs: Whether throughput is healthy or being spent on trustworthiness. Watch the dip where velocity buys hardening.
metrics.healthy_direction: Sustains a roughly linear productivity rate; a hardening dip is expected, not alarming.
metrics.rationale: An org-level target: sustain linear productivity as the fleet scales. A raw loop signal you steer capacity by.

metrics.name: Control growth
metrics.counts: Project-specific lint files and gate scripts, counted per window.
metrics.informs: Whether the environment is still accreting controls — one failure class at a time.
metrics.healthy_direction: Climbs steadily (lints 0 to 336 to 595 to 747; gates 0 to 20 to 76 to 102).
metrics.rationale: A trajectory target: keep accreting controls as failure classes surface. The governance apparatus, measured as it grows.

metrics.name: Churn
metrics.counts: Lines added and deleted per week per path.
metrics.informs: Which phase the build is in. A churn peak marks mechanization; its collapse marks a stabilizing environment.
metrics.healthy_direction: Peaks at mechanization, then collapses as the environment stabilizes.
metrics.rationale: A useful loop signal: reads out the build phase you are in, so you know whether to expect rewrite or stability.

metrics.name: MBSE navigation token-savings
metrics.counts: Tokens spent to reach an answer, with the model on versus off.
metrics.informs: The model's payoff in context budget.
metrics.rationale: A model-payoff diagnostic, not a target. You measure it to justify the model, but you do not steer the build by it.

metrics.name: Model-sync efficacy
metrics.counts: Whether the drift and parity gates keep model equal to code.
metrics.rationale: A gate and invariant health-check, not a steering target. A binary you keep green, not a number you drive toward a goal.

metrics.name: Grammar coverage
metrics.counts: Whether the generator exercised every production of the input grammar.
metrics.informs: Corpus richness — a hole no line-coverage number reveals.
metrics.rationale: A technique-local generative-validation oracle in the coverage family, not an org-level target for the whole program.

metrics.name: Model-claim coverage
metrics.counts: Whether generated inputs drove the invariants, transitions, and edges the model declares.
metrics.informs: The saturation oracle for generative validation.
metrics.rationale: A technique-local saturation oracle for generative validation, not an org-level target you steer the program by.
